name: BeEST
full_name: Beryllium Electron capture in Superconducting Tunnel junctions experiment
summary: BeEST searches for heavy sterile-neutrino admixtures through recoil spectroscopy of beryllium-7 electron capture. Radioactive atoms are embedded in superconducting quantum sensors.
detection_principle: A 7Be atom captures an electron and recoils as 7Li. An implanted superconducting tunnel junction measures recoil and atomic de-excitation energy. A heavy-neutrino admixture would shift part of the recoil distribution; material effects and atomic final states must be modelled.

sites.name: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, California; published Phase-II measurement
sites.location: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, California; published Phase-II measurement

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: The first sterile-neutrino search was followed by the 36-pixel Phase-III programme. TRIUMF supplied isotope production and implantation; the cited Phase-II recoil measurement was performed at LLNL.

collaboration.name: BeEST Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

results.summary: Published laboratory limits on sub-MeV sterile-neutrino admixtures.
Documented signal processing and spectral modelling for the larger Phase-III sensor array.

science_scope: A recoil-spectrum distortion tests a heavy-neutrino admixture; it is not automatically an active-neutrino mass measurement or proof of cosmological dark matter.
